text:
ashley: FYI seeing a cluster of pending tiny-gang pods stuck in us-west2-rack3. Lots of 0.5/1 GPU allocations scattered instead of packing, and we've entered a soft-evict loop on some nodes. Noticed NIC p95 on warmpool-3-* jumped to ~220ms around 09:15 UTC. :thinking_face:

matt: ugh. Could you grab `kubectl describe pod` for one of the pending tiny-gang pods and one node? Curious if it's node scoring / taint related.

ashley: pasted snippets:
```
$ kubectl describe pod mini-gang-9 -n batch
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x10 over 6m)  default-scheduler  0/120 nodes are available: 44 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 76 node(s) didn't have enough free GPUs.

$ kubectl describe node warmpool-3-06
Conditions: Ready=True
Taints: gpu/warmpool:NoSchedule
Network: p95=230ms, p50=35ms, errors=0
```

leo: pattern matches earlier interconnect blips. When the scheduler penalty for interconnect rises, score favors spread to nodes with lower score but more fragmentation. Result = many small free slots across racks.

sarah: short mitigations to consider: lower topologySpreadWeight for tiny-gangs to bias binpacking, untaint a handful of warm nodes in the affected rack so scheduler has compact spots, or run a targeted descheduler to coalesce.

jordan: descheduler is safest if dry-run looks OK. Evicting during high NIC latency could hurt latency for in-flight jobs, so we should cap evictions and monitor tail latencies.

ashley: plan of attack (will do canary on rack3 only):
- change Deployment for test tiny-gang set: make anti-affinity `preferredDuringScheduling` instead of `required`
- untaint warmpool-3-03/3-04 for 15m via `kubectl patch node` so scheduler can place compactly
- run descheduler in dry-run mode with compact-policy.yaml, evaluate candidates
- if dry-run looks safe, run descheduler with `--eviction-rate=20m` limit and monitor evictions

deploy-bot: initiating configmap rollout: scheduler.topologyWeightDefaults.antiAffinity=50 (canary=true, region=us-west2-rack3)

matt: please paste dry-run output. Also make sure SRE alert thresholds are primed: `evictions_per_min` and `pod_restart_rate`.

ashley: dry-run output:
```
I0410 09:27:02 descheduler: found 46 candidate evictions; would compact into 12 nodes; median free GPU per target=1.5; candidates are mostly tiny-gang-* and a few low-priority training jobs
Recommendation: evict 30 low-priority pods to coalesce slot fragments.
```

sre-bot: incident INF-5632 created: "us-west2 rack3 NIC p95 oscillation causing scheduler fragmentation" assigned to eng-platform. Priority=P3.

leo: if we go forward, throttle descheduler evictions and prefer evicting non-NVLink-critical jobs first. Also watch for pci/driver flaps in node logs.

jordan: estimate: if packing succeeds we should see ~10-15% drop in GPU-hours for batch queue over the next day. Watch billing dashboard.

ashley: applied untaint and patched the canary affinity. Monitoring: 8 minutes after changes pending queue down 65%, `gpu_fragmentation_index` down from 0.42 -> 0.28, NIC p95 for untainted nodes back to ~50ms. No user-facing errors so far.

sarah: nice. Follow-up: add a conditional into autoscaler that only relaxes anti-affinity when `interconnect.p95 < 100ms` for 5m window, and add a runbook step to prefer descheduler dry-run before any global affinity change.

ashley: filing RFC for autoscaler guard and runbook. Leaving canary running 2h then promote if stable. Rolling back if evictions > 200 within 10m or if job latency SLO breaches. :thumbsup:
